text.p: The UK High Court on Monday overturned the conviction of Elizabeth Forsyth former aide to Asil Nadir, the Cypriot business tycoon and founder of bankrupt firm Poly Peck.
Forsyth was sentenced in April last year to five years in prison after being convicted of two offences of handling stolen goods.
Lord Justice Beldam said: "We hold that her conviction is unsafe and that her appeal should be allowed".
The reason the conviction was overturned was because the judge was ruled to have misdirected the jury, the judge said.
"I'm very grateful to the court of appeal for so firmly redressing this miscarriage of justice and restoring my good name," Forsyth said.
She said her conviction had not been quashed on technical grounds but because of the merits of the defence.
"The SFO has tried to ruin my life, I hope they shall offer compensation for 10 months of wrongful imprisonment," she said.
She said she would take legal advice on how to secure compensation if the SFO did not act.
